sections.content: If you've been priced out of Seattle or simply looking for stronger cash flow numbers, real estate deals in Everett WA deserve a serious look. Located just 25 miles north of Seattle along the I-5 corridor, Everett is the seat of Snohomish County and home to roughly 116,000 residents. It offers investors a rare combination: a growing economy, improving infrastructure, and home prices that still trail the Seattle metro by a meaningful margin. Whether you're a wholesaler, a house flipper, or a buy-and-hold landlord, Everett has opportunity across every strategy. If you're just getting started, check out our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving in.
Everett WA Market Overview: What Investors Need to Know

Everett's economy is anchored by Boeing's massive manufacturing campus, Naval Station Everett, and a growing healthcare and tech sector. These employers create a stable base of working-class and middle-income renters and buyers, which is exactly what real estate investors want to see. The city has also been investing heavily in its downtown waterfront redevelopment, new transit links, and mixed-use development projects that are attracting younger residents and pushing property values upward. This combination of stable employment and active development makes Everett one of the more resilient markets in the Pacific Northwest when the broader market softens.
Average Home Prices in Everett WA

As of late 2024, the median home price in Everett sits around $520,000 to $545,000, roughly 30 to 35 percent below Seattle's median. That gap creates real opportunity for investors who can buy distressed or off-market properties in the $380,000 to $450,000 range, add value, and sell or rent at market rates. Average days on market hover around 18 to 25 days for move-in-ready homes, while fixer-uppers and distressed properties often sit longer — sometimes 45 to 60 days — giving investors more negotiating room. Rent rates for a three-bedroom single-family home average between $2,200 and $2,600 per month depending on condition and neighborhood, which supports reasonable cash flow in many buy-and-hold scenarios.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Everett

Not all of Everett's neighborhoods offer the same investor upside. Knowing where to focus your energy will save you time and money. Here's a breakdown of the areas generating the most investor activity right now on [our Everett WA market page](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/everett-wa).

items: Downtown Everett & Waterfront District: Undergoing rapid redevelopment. Great for buy-and-hold investors targeting young professionals and renters priced out of Seattle. Condo and multi-family opportunities abound, though competition is increasing.

Pinehurst / Holly: A working-class neighborhood with solid rental demand and lower entry prices in the $380,000 to $430,000 range. Strong candidate for wholesale and flip deals due to aging housing stock.
Riverside: One of the more affordable pockets in Everett. Single-family homes here often need cosmetic updates but produce strong rent-to-price ratios. Good for BRRRR strategy investors.
North Everett: Close to Boeing and the naval station, making it a reliable rental area with low vacancy. Value-add duplexes and small multi-family properties surface here regularly.
Silver Lake / Everett Heights: A step up in price but closer to suburban amenities. Ideal for flippers targeting end buyers who want move-in-ready homes in the $550,000 to $620,000 range.

sections.content: Pro Tip: Focus your first few deals in neighborhoods within a 10-minute drive of Boeing's Everett campus or Naval Station Everett. Steady employment in those areas keeps vacancy low and renter demand consistent, even when the broader market cools.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Everett WA
Wholesale Deals

Everett has a healthy wholesale market, particularly in older neighborhoods where homeowners have lived for 20 to 30 years and may be facing deferred maintenance, probate situations, or financial hardship. Wholesale assignment fees in this market typically run between $15,000 and $35,000 depending on the deal. To make the numbers work, you need to find properties where the ARV supports a purchase price well below market. Use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to run comps quickly and make sure your offer leaves enough room for your buyer's rehab costs and profit margin. If you're new to the process, our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide walks you through every step.
Fix and Flip Deals

Flipping houses in Everett can be profitable, but margins require discipline. The typical flip in Everett targets homes purchased in the $380,000 to $440,000 range, with rehab budgets between $40,000 and $80,000 for cosmetic to moderate renovations, and resale prices in the $540,000 to $620,000 range. That leaves gross profit potential of $50,000 to $100,000 before carrying costs, agent fees, and financing. The key is buying right. Always run your numbers with a tool like our [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) before making any offer. Everett buyers in this price range expect updated kitchens, modern bathrooms, and fresh finishes — cutting corners on the finish level here will cost you on the back end.
Rental and BRRRR Strategy

Long-term rentals are where Everett's steady employment base really shines for investors. With average rents between $2,200 and $2,600 for a three-bedroom home and purchase prices for distressed properties starting around $390,000, cash flow is tight but achievable — especially with a 25 percent down payment and a value-add component. The BRRRR strategy (Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat) works particularly well in Riverside and North Everett, where forced appreciation through renovation can push values up 15 to 20 percent after a solid rehab. Small multi-family properties — duplexes and triplexes — offer even better cash flow math and surface in Everett more regularly than in the tighter Seattle market.
Everett WA Real Estate Market Trends in 2024

Everett's market has shown resilience in 2024 despite elevated interest rates. Inventory remains tight across Snohomish County, with active listings running 20 to 25 percent below pre-pandemic norms. Price appreciation has moderated from the 15 to 20 percent annual gains of 2021 and 2022, but values have held steady and are trending slightly upward year-over-year. The most important trend for investors to watch is the continued Seattle overflow effect: as Seattle rents and prices stay elevated, more renters and first-time buyers are moving north to Everett, strengthening demand across every property type. Light rail expansion plans connecting Everett to Seattle's Link system are also a long-term tailwind that could meaningfully increase property values near future station areas.

"The cities that outperform over the long run are almost always the ones sitting in the shadow of a major metro — close enough to benefit from the economic engine, but still affordable enough for real demand to exist." — Common wisdom among experienced Pacific Northwest investors
Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Everett

Everett is attracting growing interest from California, Nevada, and Arizona investors looking to deploy capital in a stable Pacific Northwest market. Here's how to navigate the market effectively if you're investing from a distance.

items: Build a local team first: Before making any offers, line up a local real estate agent who works with investors, a reliable general contractor, and a property manager. Everett has a tight contractor market, so securing relationships early matters.

Target off-market deals: The best real estate deals in Everett WA rarely hit the MLS. Direct mail, driving for dollars (using a local birddogger), and probate leads are your best sources. Read our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) for proven strategies.
Understand Washington State landlord-tenant law: Washington has strong tenant protections that affect eviction timelines and lease requirements. Educate yourself before your first rental purchase.

Account for Seattle contractor pricing: Labor costs in the greater Seattle metro are higher than most U.S. markets. Budget $50 to $70 per square foot for mid-level renovations and $80 to $100 per square foot for higher-end finishes.

Analyze every deal thoroughly: Never rely on gut feel alone. Learn [how to analyze real estate deals like a pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) using consistent metrics — cap rate, cash-on-cash return, and MAO (Maximum Allowable Offer) — before committing to any purchase.

Visit at least once before scaling: Even seasoned remote investors benefit from spending two to three days walking neighborhoods, meeting their team in person, and getting a feel for micro-market differences between ZIP codes.

sections.content: Pro Tip: When reaching out to sellers in Everett, reference local landmarks and community context in your letters or calls. Sellers respond better to buyers who clearly know the area — even if you're calling from out of state. Mention Boeing, the waterfront, or specific neighborhood names to build credibility fast.
Is Everett WA Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Everett is not a market where you'll find $100,000 homes or 15 percent cash-on-cash returns straight off the MLS. But it's also not a speculative long shot. It's a market backed by real employment, growing infrastructure, and a steady flow of Seattle spillover demand that shows no sign of reversing. For wholesalers, there are distressed properties and motivated sellers. For flippers, there's a strong buyer pool and rising ARVs. For landlords, there's dependable rental demand from Boeing workers, military families, and service industry workers. With the right systems in place and careful deal analysis, Everett offers a realistic path to consistent, repeatable returns in one of the most economically stable regions in the country.
